---- Applicant Versus
1. State Of Chhattisgarh, Through Station House Officer, Police Station City Kotwali, Bilaspur,
District Bilaspur (C.G.).
---- Non-applicant For Applicant : Mr. Prahalad Panda, Advocate.

For Non-Applicant/State : Mr.
Ashish Tiwari, G.A. Hon'ble Shri Justice Radhakishan Agrawal Order on Board 20/01/2023 1) The applicant has preferred this First Bail Application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, as he in jail since 22/07/2020 in connection with Crime No. 182/2019 registered at Police Station Sirgitti, Bilaspur, District Bilaspur (C.G.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.

2) Allegation against the present applicant is that he alongwith other co-accused Rajesh Kumar Sharma and Ravi @ Ravi Patnaik fraudulently obtained Rs. 8,94,125/- as a C.C. loan from Punjab Bank in the name of complainant Kishore Sahu.
On report being lodged to the above effect, the aforesaid offences have been registered against the accused persons.
3) Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.

He also submits that the co-accused Rajesh Kumar Sharma has already been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 06/09/2019 passed in MCRC No. 5194/2019 and Ravishankar @ Ravi Patnaik has already been granted bail by the Trial Court vide order dated 29/10/2020.
He submits that the applicant is in jail since 22/07/2020 (i.e. more than 2 years & 5 months).
He submits that charge sheet has been filed but charges have not yet been framed.
He submits that there is no apprehension of the applicant tampering with the evidence or absconding and conclusion of trial is likely to take some time for its disposal.
Therefore, the applicant be released on bail by this Court on the ground of parity.
4) On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
He submits that applicant has some previous criminal antecedents.

sentences.text:
Having heard learned counsel for the parties, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, the detention period of the applicant (i.e. more than 2 years and 5 months) who is 50 years old,
charge sheet has already been filed but charges have not yet been framed, co-accused persons have already been granted bail by this Court and the Trial Court, there is no apprehension of the applicant tampering with the evidence or absconding as admitted by both the Counsel and that conclusion of trial may take some time, without commenting anything on merits of the case, this Court is of the opinion that present is a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the application is allowed.

6) It is directed that applicant shall be released on regular bail, on his furnishing a bail bond in sum of Rs. 50,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the said Court.

He shall be released on bail on the following conditions:-
i. he shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such fact to the Court

, ii. he shall not act in any manner which will be prejudicial to fair and expeditious trial, iii. he shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date given to him by the said Court till disposal of the trial, iv. he shall not involve himself in any offence of similar nature in future.

-Sd/-
(Radhakishan Agrawal) Judge Chandrakant Vishwajit Bhaumik vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/182536165/
